title: Add XY Heatmap Chart Mark

complexity.rationale: This reuses two already-precedented pieces once add-histogram-mark and add-heatmap-mark land: Vega's `bin` transform (applied to two continuous fields instead of one) plus a count aggregate, and a rect-per-cell mark with a sequential color scale (the same addSequentialColorScale helper Heatmap introduces). No new algorithm is needed — only combining two existing patterns across two axes instead of one.

summary: A two-continuous-variable density grid mark — bins x and y into a grid via Vega's `bin` transform on both axes, aggregates a count per cell, and renders with a sequential color scale. Kept as a distinct mark/chartType from the categorical Heatmap per its own quantitative-binned axes.
requirements: Accepts `x`, `y` (both continuous/quantitative, required) channels — no pre-existing categories
Bins both x and y into equal-width buckets via Vega's `bin` transform (extending add-histogram-mark's single-axis bin approach to two axes), then aggregates a `count` per x-bin/y-bin combination
Renders one rect per populated bin combination, reusing Heatmap's rect-mark construction pattern but keyed by bin boundaries instead of ordinal row/column values
Cell fill color is driven by the same sequential color scale approach introduced for Heatmap, over the count domain

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Degenerate bin extent on both axes — falls back to a single bin per axis, matching Histogram's degenerate-extent handling.
Only populated bins render rects; empty combinations are simply absent, not rendered as zero-count cells.
Excluded from binning, consistent with Histogram's null-handling.

edgeCases.case: Very large datasets (many points, fine bins)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Aggregation happens once via the Vega transform pipeline at render time; no client-side pre-aggregation needed, consistent with how other marks let Vega handle transforms.
Sequential color scale range is theme-aware, matching Heatmap.
S1-only for this spec; no S2 port until the mark stabilizes out of rc status.

crossCutting.notes: touchesHoverAnimation: reuses the standard rect-mark hover encode; the 1.08x hover scale-up from add-heatmap-mark can be reused directly since the mark shape is the same. touchesTooltipOrPopover: cells support ChartTooltip/ChartPopover showing bin range/count, reusing existing interactive-mark plumbing. requiresNewSignalOrScale: true — reuses add-heatmap-mark's addSequentialColorScale helper (shared scale-builder, separate scale instance) plus two binned-linear axis scales (not ordinal band scales, since axes are continuous). requiresS1S2Parity: false because this ships as a new s1-only rc-status mark, matching the Donut/BigNumber precedent; revisit once promoted out of rc.

addTwoAxisBinTransform (applies add-histogram-mark's bin-transform approach to both x and y, then an aggregate count per bin-pair) — extends the histogram spec's single-axis pattern to two axes rather than duplicating it from scratch.
getXyHeatmapCellMark, reusing add-heatmap-mark's getHeatmapCellMark rect-mark construction but keyed by bin0/bin1 fields on both axes instead of ordinal row/column.

addXyHeatmap, addData (calls addTwoAxisBinTransform), addSignals (reuse interactive-mark signal helpers), setScales (two binned-linear axis scales, calls add-heatmap-mark's addSequentialColorScale for count).
Unit tests for addTwoAxisBinTransform, including the degenerate-extent case.
Unit tests for getXyHeatmapCellMark using the fixture.

XyHeatmapProps/XyHeatmapElement, Omit-ing only fields replaced at the React boundary (ChartTooltip/ChartPopover children).
Render-null component holding prop defaults, placed under rc/ per the Donut/BigNumber rc-status precedent.
Import XyHeatmap from '../rc' and add its displayName dispatch case.
Add XyHeatmap to the sanitizeRscChartChildren import/list from '../rc'.
Update the toStrictEqual ChartOptions snapshot to include the new mark type at default values.
Basic story with a two-continuous-variable dataset.

openQuestions: Should maxBins be independently configurable per axis, or a single shared value for both x and y?

Sequencing: should this wait for add-histogram-mark's bin-transform helper and add-heatmap-mark's sequential-scale helper to land first so this spec can directly reuse them, rather than reimplementing either?
